meta.note: Definitions in this repo's own words, written for a returning player. They describe the mechanics that have been stable across the last two editions; the July 2026 briefing recorded three changes for the current edition (cover makes a target harder to hit rather than improving its save, quiet infantry in terrain cannot be seen beyond 15 inches, and a unit benefits from one stratagem per phase). Read the core rules once; the app is the arbiter.

terms.def: How many inches the unit moves with a Normal move in the Movement phase. Advancing adds D6 inches but bars shooting and charging unless a rule says otherwise; here the Khorne boon and Assault weapons say otherwise.
How hard the model is to wound. The attack's Strength is compared against it to set the wound roll.
The armour save: roll this or better on a D6 to ignore a wound. The attack's AP makes it worse. A 7+ means no armour save at all; the model lives on its invulnerable save.
How much damage a model absorbs before it is destroyed. Damage from one attack never spills onto the next model, except mortal wounds.
The target for Battle-shock and Leadership tests: roll 2D6 and pass on that number or more, so 6+ is better than 7+. Daemonic Icons set it to 6+.
The weight a model adds when contesting an objective marker. Whoever has more total OC within 3 inches controls it. OC 0 can stand on a marker forever and never own it.
A save that AP cannot modify. Use it whenever it is better than the modified armour save. Most of this army has a 4+ or 5+ and no armour to speak of.
How far the weapon reaches, measured base to base. Melee means it is used only in engagement range.
How many dice the weapon rolls to hit. D6 or D3 means roll for the number each time it fires.
The to-hit roll for shooting. N/A means the weapon hits automatically (a Torrent weapon).
The to-hit roll for melee.
Compared with the target's Toughness to set the wound roll: double it or more wounds on 2+, higher on 3+, equal on 4+, lower on 5+, half or less on 6+.
Subtracted from the target's armour save: AP-2 turns a 3+ into a 5+. It never touches an invulnerable save.
Wounds removed from one model per unsaved hit. Damage beyond that model's remaining wounds is lost, which is why one-wound daemons do not care about D2.
The weapon can be fired in a turn the unit Advanced.
+1 to hit if the unit did not move this turn.
Can be fired while in engagement range, at an enemy unit the bearer is engaged with. A model with a pistol and another gun fires one or the other.
Rapid Fire X: the weapon gains X extra attacks against targets within half its range.
Hits automatically, no hit roll. That is why Torrent weapons are the ones worth Overwatching with, since Overwatch otherwise only hits on 6s.
+1 attack per five models in the target unit, and it cannot be fired at a unit within engagement range of your own models.
The target gets no benefit of cover against the attack.
A critical hit (an unmodified 6 to hit) wounds automatically, skipping the wound roll.
Sustained Hits X: a critical hit scores X extra hits on top of itself.
A critical wound (an unmodified 6 to wound) inflicts its damage as mortal wounds: no armour save, no invulnerable save.
When the target is a unit with a Character attached, the attacker may put the hit on the Character instead of the bodyguard.

Anti-X Y+: against a target with keyword X, an unmodified wound roll of Y or more counts as a critical wound. With Devastating Wounds that means mortal wounds; the Screamers' bites carry Anti-Monster and Anti-Vehicle 4+.
+1 to wound in a turn the unit charged. The Juggernauts' horns.
Re-roll the wound roll.
The weapon's attacks are made in addition to the model's other melee weapon, not instead of it.

After the weapon is used, roll a D6 for each Hazardous weapon fired: on a 1 the bearer suffers 3 mortal wounds, or is destroyed if it has one wound. The focused witchfire profiles are Hazardous; the base profiles are not.
The attack counts as psychic. That matters for Anti-Psyker weapons, the Flesh Hounds' collars, and any Feel No Pain that names psychic attacks.
Can target a unit the bearer cannot see, at -1 to hit and with the target counting as in cover.
Melta X: +X damage against a target within half range.
An unmodified 6 on the hit roll (critical hit) or the wound roll (critical wound). The trigger for Lethal Hits, Sustained Hits, Devastating Wounds and Anti-X.

The unit may start in Reserves and, from the second battle round, arrive at the end of your Movement phase anywhere more than 9 inches from enemy models. Warp Rifts trims that to 6 inches for daemons arriving inside the shadow or beside their own god's Greater Daemon. The detachment hands Deep Strike to the marines too.
Scouts X inches: before the first turn the unit may move up to X inches, ending more than 9 inches from the enemy. Leaping Shadows grants Scouts 9.
The unit may be deployed anywhere on the table more than 9 inches from the enemy deployment zone and from enemy models. The Nurglings' whole job.
Enemy ranged attacks against the unit hit at -1. The Tzeentch boon gives it to every Tzeentch daemon here.
Feel No Pain X+: each time the model would lose a wound, roll a D6; on X or more the wound is not lost. It works against mortal wounds too unless the ability says otherwise.
Deadly Demise X: when the model is destroyed, roll a D6; on a 6 every unit within 6 inches suffers X mortal wounds. The monsters all have it.
The unit fights in the Fight phase before units without it, even when the enemy charged.

A Character with Leader may be attached to one of its listed units before the battle. They move and fight as one unit, and the Character cannot be shot out of it (except by Precision) while bodyguards remain.
An ability that affects every eligible unit within its range, the bearer's own unit included. Be'lakor's three Shadow Forms and the Greater Daemons' bubbles are auras.
Cannot be shot from more than 12 inches away unless it is part of an attached unit. No unit in this collection has it.
The bracket at which a big model starts hitting worse, usually -1 to hit for its last third of wounds.
Foot models. They can move through and hide in terrain that stops others, and are what Blast and screens are for.
Cavalry: Bloodcrushers, Plague Drones, the Skullmaster, the Rendmaster and the Fateskimmer. Faster, tougher, and without the Infantry terrain rules.
Fast animals: Flesh Hounds, Screamers, Beasts of Nurgle. They move through terrain like Infantry.
The Nurglings: bases of many small creatures counted as one model each.
The big models: Be'lakor, the Greater Daemons, the Daemon Prince. They can shoot while in engagement range, cannot hide behind most terrain, and are what Anti-Monster weapons hunt.
The War Dogs. The Shadow Legion admits no Vehicles, which is why they attend as Dreadblades instead.
Can move over models and terrain as if they were not there, measuring the move across the top. Screamers' Slashing Dive and the monsters' mobility depend on it.
A hero model. Only Characters carry enhancements, and a Character with Leader can join a unit. Attached, it cannot be picked out except by Precision.
A named Character: one per army, no enhancements. The Shadow Legion bans every Epic Hero except Be'lakor, which is why Skulltaker and Karanak are out.

The army's core troops: up to six of one Battleline datasheet instead of three, and here the unit type that gets destroyed models back from Daemonic Manifestation. Pink and Blue Horrors, Bloodletters, Nurglings, Legionaries and Cultists.
A model that uses Psychic abilities, and the target Anti-Psyker weapons want. Be'lakor, the Lord of Change, the Great Unclean One, the Fateskimmer, the Master of Possession and the Horrors.
The keyword shared by every Legiones Daemonica model, and by the Possessed and Warp Talons. Legiones Daemonica is the faction keyword that the army rules and Warp Rifts key off.
The Chaos Daemons faction keyword. The army rules, Warp Rifts and the Greater Daemons' auras apply to units with it; the marines do not have it.
The Chaos Space Marines faction keyword. In this detachment those units gain Dark Pacts and Deep Strike, and together they may make up at most half the army.
The unit may use the Grenades stratagem: a nearby enemy unit takes mortal wounds on dice rolls of 4+. The marines have it; the daemons do not.
The model that leads the army; some missions and abilities key off it. Here it must be Be'lakor whenever he is in the list.
One player turn each. Games run five battle rounds. Reinforcements may arrive from the second.

The start of your turn: gain 1 CP, take Battle-shock tests for units below half strength, and resolve abilities that trigger here. Primary objectives are scored at the start of it from the second round.

A test taken in the Command phase by units below half strength, and whenever a rule forces one: roll 2D6 and pass on your Leadership or more. A failed unit is Battle-shocked until your next Command phase: OC 0, no stratagems on it, and Desperate Escape tests if it Falls Back. This army makes the enemy take many of these at -1, and its own daemons pass at +1 and heal.

A unit with fewer than half its starting models, or a single model with fewer than half its wounds. Such units test Battle-shock each Command phase; Be'lakor's Pall of Despair forces tests on enemy units that are merely below Starting Strength.
Moving up to the Move characteristic. The unit may still shoot and charge afterwards.

Move plus D6 inches, at the cost of shooting and charging that turn unless a rule allows it. Assault weapons may still fire; Khorne daemons here may still charge (Murderer's Cowl); Warp Surge lets a daemon in the shadow charge too.

Moving out of engagement range. The unit cannot shoot or charge afterwards unless a rule allows it, and Battle-shocked units must take Desperate Escape tests to do it. Flamers may shoot after Falling Back.
Within 1 inch of an enemy model. Units in it fight in the Fight phase and can only shoot Pistols.

Declare targets, roll 2D6, and move that far to get into engagement range with every target, or the charge fails and the unit stays where it was. A unit arriving 9 inches from the enemy needs a 9 on 2D6, which succeeds about a quarter of the time; from 6 inches it needs a 6, which succeeds more often than not.
Units that charged fight first, then the players alternate. Each unit piles in up to 3 inches, makes its attacks, and consolidates up to 3 inches (6 with a Bloodmaster).
The 3-inch move after fighting, towards the nearest enemy or an objective marker. A Bloodmaster's unit moves 6.

Roll to hit against BS or WS, roll to wound with Strength against Toughness, the defender rolls the better of its modified armour save and its invulnerable save, then Damage comes off Wounds. Mortal wounds skip the whole thing.

Strength against Toughness: double or more wounds on 2+, higher on 3+, equal on 4+, lower on 5+, half or less on 6+. A Bloodletter's S5 hellblade wounds a T4 marine on 3+, a T5 marine on 4+, a T12 Knight on 6+.

Damage that skips the hit roll, wound roll and every save. Each mortal wound removes one wound, and they spill over to the next model. Only Feel No Pain stops them. This army deals them through Battle-shock failures, Devastating Wounds, Brass Stampede, Slashing Dive and Relentless Carnage.

Units held off the table. They arrive from the second battle round: Strategic Reserves at a table edge, Deep Strike units anywhere 9 inches from the enemy. The mission pack caps how much of the army may start in Reserves; check it before writing the whole army off the board.

The core stratagem (1 CP) that lets a unit in Reserves arrive at the end of the opponent's Movement phase instead of your own. The return half of the yo-yo; free for a Chaos Lord's own squad once per round.

The core stratagem (1 CP) that lets a unit shoot at an enemy unit that moves or charges within 24 inches of it, in the enemy's turn. It hits only on unmodified 6s, so Torrent weapons, which hit automatically, are the ones that make it hurt.
The core stratagem that lets one of your units charge an enemy unit that just charged near it, in the enemy's Charge phase.
When a Battle-shocked unit Falls Back, or a unit leaves the Bloodletters' Bane of Cowards, roll a D6 per model: on a 1 or 2 that model is destroyed.
The currency for stratagems: one gained each Command phase. Per the July briefing, a unit benefits from only one stratagem per phase this edition.
A one-off rule bought with CP in the moment. Core stratagems are shared by every army (Rapid Ingress, Overwatch, Grenades, Command Re-roll); detachment stratagems are the Shadow Legion's own.

An upgrade bought with points for one Character that is not an Epic Hero: each enhancement once per army, at most three in total. Fade to Darkness, Leaping Shadows, Mantle of Gloom and Malice Made Manifest are the Shadow Legion's.

The army's rules package: a rule, enhancements and stratagems. This edition prices detachments in Detachment Points so two can be combined; the tournament lists pair Shadow Legion (2 DP) with Cavalcade of Chaos (1 DP).
A unit can be targeted if any part of one of its models can be seen from the attacker. The Rendmaster's Blood Throne and most shooting need it.

What terrain gives a target. Per the July briefing, in this edition it makes the target harder to hit rather than improving its save, and quiet infantry inside terrain cannot be seen from beyond 15 inches. Read the core rules for the exact wording.
The points on the table you score for controlling, contested within 3 inches by Objective Control. Killing the enemy is only ever a means to standing on more of these.

The primary is the mission's fixed scoring, usually holding markers at the start of your Command phase. Secondaries are the extra goals drawn or chosen each game: actions, kills, positions. Both matter; most games are lost on the secondaries.
A task a unit performs instead of shooting or charging to score a secondary. The Legionaries' second job.

The disposition the Shadow Legion's missions use, as the July briefing described it: extra points each round for destroying more enemy units than you lose. Cheap screens that die for nothing feed it to the opponent.
Your third of the table at the start; the opponent's is theirs. The Shadow of Chaos begins in yours and spreads to No Man's Land and then to theirs as you take their markers.
The middle of the table between the deployment zones, where most of the objectives sit. Hold half of its markers at the start of a phase and it is inside your shadow for that phase.
The 2,000-point game size, the one every list in this repo is built to.
Every unit's cost, set by the Munitorum Field Manual and updated a few times a year. Every number in this repo carries a snapshot date because of that.
What you see is what you get: the models must carry the weapons the list says. Tournaments enforce it; kitchen tables do not.

The army rule's zone: your deployment zone always, No Man's Land and the enemy zone when you hold half their markers, and 6 inches around Be'lakor and each Greater Daemon. Inside it your daemons pass Battle-shock at +1 and heal or regrow; enemies test at -1 and bleed mortal wounds.
The per-god ability the Shadow Legion gives every unit: Murderer's Cowl (Khorne), Penumbral Puppetry (Tzeentch), Gloam Rot (Nurgle), Disciples of Be'lakor (Undivided).

Kill, vanish, return: a unit with Fade to Darkness (or the Warp Talons' Warp Strike) kills something, leaves the table at the end of the Fight phase, and comes back by Rapid Ingress in the opponent's turn. Mallex's Legionaries and the Bloodthirster are the carriers.
A full ten-model unit with its Herald attached, here almost always a Bloodmaster and ten Bloodletters.
A unit that deep-strikes to kill one thing and does not expect to survive the reply: the Possessed with the Master of Possession.
The defensive cluster in your own half: Horrors, Flamers, Havocs and Cultists packed under a monster's bubble so everything benefits from every aura at once.
Cheap units placed to block charges and deep-strike lanes so the valuable units cannot be reached: Nurglings and Cultists here. Chaff is the same idea said less kindly.
An aura's radius, 6 inches for almost everything here. Be'lakor's and the Greater Daemons' bubbles carry the shadow with them.
Winning by hitting first, on turn one, before the opponent's plan exists. List D is built for it; it wins on turn two or loses on turn three.
Exchanging one of your units for one of theirs. Trading a 45-point screen for a 200-point charge is the Purge the Foe arithmetic done right.
The Chaos Knights rule that lets up to three War Dogs join any all-Chaos army without joining its detachment: no Warlord, no enhancements, no Shadow Legion boons. Verify it before a tournament.

The list of Chaos Space Marine units the Shadow Legion may take: Chaos Lords, Sorcerers, Master of Possession, Dark Apostle, Legionaries, Chosen, Possessed, Raptors, Warp Talons, Havocs and Damned units. Chaos Terminators are not on it.
A second, 1 DP detachment the tournament lists pair with the Shadow Legion, and the source of Soul-shattering Charge. Its rules were never captured in this repo.
A Bloodthirster carrying Fade to Darkness, and the name of list E, the tournament shape every 4-1 result the July research studied shares.

The Chaos Space Marines army rule, which this detachment lends to Be'lakor and every marine: test Leadership when the unit shoots or fights, take D3 mortal wounds on a failure, and either way its weapons gain Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 for the phase.

The Chaos Daemons rule that lets a daemon deep-striking inside the shadow, or beside its own god's Greater Daemon, arrive 6 inches from the enemy instead of 9. A 6-inch charge succeeds far more often than a 9.

Half of the Shadow of Chaos rule: a daemon unit inside the shadow adds 1 to its Battle-shock roll and, on a pass, heals D3 wounds or, if Battleline, returns up to D3 destroyed models. The Horrors' and Bloodletters' resurrection engine.
The other half: an enemy unit inside the shadow, or within 6 inches of a Greater Daemon, takes Battle-shock tests at -1 and suffers D3 mortal wounds when it fails.
